title: Contextual Autodiag Prober and Safe-Guarded Runbook Suggestor
author: Priya Nambiar
description:
Motivation: On-call responders need fast, targeted diagnostics for noisy alerts without triggering unsafe automated mitigations. This PR adds a Contextual Autodiag Prober that runs a prioritized, low-impact set of probes (metric queries, tail-sampled logs, short traces, and a lightweight synthetic request) based on alert fingerprints and SLO burn signals. It also introduces a Safety-Guarded Runbook Suggestor that ranks playbook actions and prevents high-impact automated remediations unless explicit conditions are met (confidence threshold, canary confirmation, and human approval for critical mitigations).

What this changes (high level): Adds a new prober subsystem in incident-bot that queries SLO burn-rates (via slo-toolkit adapter), selects probes by cost/impact score, and assembles an evidence bundle for the runbook suggester. The runbook suggester computes an action score and suppresses automated mitigation when the safety guard detects high blast-radius or insufficient telemetry coverage. A small CLI command (incidentctl prefetch) lets responders pre-warm the prober before a shift or during a postmortem.

Key behaviors: - Prioritization heuristic: weight by alert severity, recent error velocity, and correlation with high-cardinality dimensions. - Safe mitigation gating: mitigations are only eligible for automated execution when (1) runbook_score >= 0.8 AND (2) canary_probe passes OR human ack present. - Ephemeral collection: all probe artifacts are TTLed after 72 hours and sanitized for PII. - Telemetry: new metrics and traces exported for probe counts, action blocks, and evidence build time.

Checklist: - [x] Core prober implementation and unit tests - [x] Safety guard + policy engine - [x] slo-toolkit adapter for burn-rate queries - [x] CLI prefetch command and docs - [x] E2E smoke in staging - [x] Security sign-off for data retention and KMS usage

Testing & rollout: Unit and integration tests exercised locally and in CI; staging run executed against a canary stack for 48h with synthetic alerts. Rollout will be staged behind a feature flag (incident.autodiag.enabled) and safety_guard defaults to conservative mode (no auto-mitigations) until product sign-off.

Notes on scope: This PR intentionally avoids adding new automated mitigation implementations (e.g., restart services). Instead it focuses on decisioning and safe gating; future PRs will wire approved mitigations through the existing action runner.

Security/privacy: Probe artifacts are encrypted at rest using existing KMS keys; the sanitizer removes user-identifying fields from logs. Audit events emitted for every suggestion and blocked action.

Related items: ENG-1257 (autodiag roadmap), SRE-423 (safety policies), SUP-987 (support case that motivated live probe abstractions).
commits: feat(prober): add contextual prober subsystem with prioritization heuristic
feat(safety): implement safety guard policy engine and blocking logic
chore(cli): incidentctl prefetch command to pre-warm probes
feat(adapter): add slo-toolkit prober adapter for burn-rate queries (mockable)
test: expand unit tests for prober and safety guard; add flakey guard in e2e to stabilize
docs: runbook suggestor design doc and rollout notes
review_comments: Ethan Morales (2026-02-22): Nice separation of concerns. Please add a migration note for the metrics name change and make the burn-rate query tolerant to partial responses. Also add a switch to opt-out of log tails in high-cardinality services.
Priya Nambiar (2026-02-23): Addressed: added metric_aliases migration and fallbacks for burn-rate; added service opt-out via annotation and test coverage for that path.

Sofia Patel (2026-02-25): Tests are failing on CI due to a race in the probe cache teardown. Can you add a deterministic clock or explicit waits? Also please add a short docs snippet about privacy sanitizer behavior.
Priya Nambiar (2026-02-26): Fixed race by using a fake clock in tests and tightened cache lifecycle; added sanitizer docs and an integration smoke run summary.

Luca Moretti (2026-03-01): Security review: confirmed KMS usage and audit events; requested a small tweak to redact IPs from synthetic request logs. Priya: updated sanitizer to remove network ids. Approved for merge.
tests_summary: Unit tests initially failed on a probe-cache race; resolved by faking the clock and adding teardown hooks. E2E smoke (staging) passed for 48h. CI lint and unit runs passing on final push after fixes; one flaky test pin removed.
release_notes: Adds a contextual autodiag prober and a safety-guarded runbook suggester. Introduces incidentctl prefetch and new metrics (incident_bot.autodiag.*). Feature is behind incident.autodiag.enabled flag and defaults to conservative mode (no auto-mitigations).
risk_assessment: low-medium: decision engine reduces risk by blocking high-impact automations by default. The safety guard requires canary confirmation or human ack before running risky actions. Monitoring and audit events added to detect misclassifications.
operational_playbook: 1) Enable feature flag in staging and run synthetic alerts against canary stack. 2) Monitor incident_bot.autodiag.blocked_actions and slo_toolkit.prober_adapter.latency; if probe latency exceeds threshold, opt-out noisy services via annotation. 3) For any unexpected auto-suggests, use incidentctl show-evidence <alert-id> to inspect collected artifacts.
notes: Differential design choice: keep mitigation implementations out of this PR to reduce blast radius and speed review. Future work will add a policy-mapped action runner plugin.
